narrative_summary: Current political and domestic tensions are intensifying as congressional Democrats weigh leveraging the upcoming government funding deadline to challenge the war in Iran and investigate administration corruption. The fallout from the recent midterm elections—marked by a significant swing toward Democrats and declining approval for Donald Trump—highlights growing public backlash against administration policies and compounding infrastructure failures, such as crippling air traffic control disruptions. Meanwhile, broader geopolitical risks persist, ranging from escalating asymmetric tactics and cyber threats abroad to fierce debates over data center developments and executive accountability at home. These converging domestic and international pressures underscore a period of profound institutional strain and heightened political confrontation.

source_summaries.title: Michael Weiss and Chris Van Hollen: Reporter and the Aspiring Majority Leader
bullets: Senator Chris Van Hollen stated that Democrats plan to investigate alleged corruption within the administration, ICE funding, and the war in Iran.
Van Hollen defended his challenge to Senator Schumer by arguing that more internal democracy is beneficial for the Senate Democratic Caucus.
Ukrainian forces successfully struck and damaged a portion of the Crimea bridge.

source_summaries.title: The First Fight of the New Senate Is Already Here
bullets: Senate Democrats hold potential leverage to force an end to the Iran war by withholding votes from the upcoming government funding legislation due in December.
Republican leaders need Democratic votes to pass the spending bill before the 120th Congress convenes in January.
Many Democratic senators have avoided committing to the hardball budget strategy despite widespread opposition to the war.

source_summaries.title: Putin’s Asymmetric War on Europe
bullets: A wave of bomb threats has disrupted commercial aviation and schools across Europe, involving hundreds of incidents linked to a sender using the initials M.A.
The Institute for the Study of War notes that these coordinated threats are designed to disrupt European society and impose economic costs.
Although not directly blamed on Russia, analysts observe that these asymmetric tactics are consistent with historical Russian strategies of intimidation and testing Western resolve.

source_summaries.title: The Axis of Evil Got an Upgrade
bullets: George W. Bush's original 2002 Axis of Evil concept grouped rogue states like Iran, Iraq, and North Korea, though they were not yet truly allied.
By 2012, a genuine illiberal axis had formed between Russia, China, and Iran to oppose the liberal world.
Russia and China have reportedly incorporated Donald Trump's United States into their coalition while maintaining their alliance with Iran.

source_summaries.title: Trump’s DHS Secretary Took Gov’t Jet to a Football Game During FAA Chaos | Morning Shots
bullets: Trump's cabinet selection prioritizes blind loyalty, questionable judgment, and incompetence.
A Trump DHS secretary used a government jet to attend a football game amid FAA chaos.
Commentators note parallels between the current administration's disconnect and the final days of the Soviet Union.

source_summaries.title: Triad Mailbag for November 27
bullets: The Bulwark is collecting reader questions for an upcoming Thanksgiving Triad Mailbag edition.
Readers are invited to submit questions, review existing submissions, and upvote topics they want addressed.
The previous Mailbag covered topics ranging from military leadership and electoral politics to personal reflections and campus culture.

source_summaries.title: Trump Can’t Even Make the Planes Run On Time
bullets: President Trump traveled to Asia for international summits while grappling with domestic criticism following recent nationwide airport chaos and outdated air traffic control systems.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy acknowledged the aging infrastructure and requested additional billions for modernization, while falsely blaming Democrats for legislative delays despite two years of full Republican control in Washington.
Donald Trump attempted to shift blame for the system failure onto the Biden administration by criticizing technical upgrades that are actually part of standard modernization efforts.

source_summaries.title: The biggest myth about American immigration policy
bullets: Critics like Stephen Miller falsely blame the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 for increasing Hispanic and Asian immigration.
The 1965 law actually imposed quantitative restrictions on immigration from Latin America that did not exist previously.
The legislation was designed to replace the discriminatory National Origins Formula of 1921 with an individual-level criteria system.

source_summaries.title: Robert Greene on Almost Dying, Finding Meaning, and Getting Off Your Phone
bullets: Author Robert Greene discussed with Scott Galloway how recovering from a near-fatal stroke influenced his worldview and his new book, The Law of the Sublime.
Greene wrote his latest book entirely by hand over seven years because the stroke left him unable to type.

The conversation also covered topics including the hesitation of young people to fall in love, the process of reconnecting with childhood perspectives, and the value of experiencing challenges in one's twenties.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: Trump’s China Strategy Backfires as Nvidia Scandal Spirals
bullets: President Trump's trip to China faces complications due to tensions surrounding advanced AI chips, Nvidia, and technological leverage.
Recent technology outages have highlighted the fragility of America's aging infrastructure.
The United States has lost its measles-elimination status for the first time in 26 years.

source_summaries.title: What’s Nvidia Worth Without Huang?
bullets: Scott Galloway and Aswath Damodaran are hosting an earnings review to analyze Nvidia's market reaction following a recent unfolding scandal.
Recent analysis from the Prof G universe questions Nvidia's succession plan and whether the company can survive without CEO Jensen Huang.
The ongoing coverage also examines broader issues including corporate governance, intellectual property theft, and workplace relationships.

source_summaries.title: Could Jensen Huang Actually Return To Nvidia?
bullets: Analysts debate whether Jensen Huang could potentially return to Nvidia.
The ongoing controversy has exposed internal divisions within the Trump administration.
Experts break down the primary risks currently facing Nvidia's stock.

source_summaries.title: Frozen at the Switch.
bullets: China is increasingly prioritizing global power projection over addressing its domestic economic weaknesses.
Recent economic data shows deteriorating domestic demand, with growth relying heavily on surging exports.
China's export-driven strategy is provoking a protectionist backlash and concerns over overcapacity from international trading partners.

source_summaries.title: Suspended in a Sunbeam.
bullets: Voyager 1 is approaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, or 25.9 billion kilometers, after nearly 49 years of travel.
Google reported that Russian-speaking hackers utilized an AI agent to execute what may be the first fully-automated cyberattack without human intervention.

source_summaries.title: A Federal Women’s Prison Became a “Rape Club.” After Officials Shut It Down, Rampant Abuse Continued Elsewhere.
bullets: A federal women's prison in Dublin, California, was shut down after rampant sexual abuse by staff led to multiple criminal convictions.
Female prisoners transferred from Dublin to a facility in Aliceville, Alabama, found that pervasive guard misconduct and sexual abuse continued there.
Despite high-profile prosecutions and subsequent government oversight reforms, inmates continue to face systemic predatory behavior within federal women's prisons.

source_summaries.title: Democrats in Washington Move to Ban Data Centers on Public Lands
bullets: A dozen congressional Democrats are pursuing legislation to limit or ban the construction of data centers on federal public lands.
The legislative push follows reporting that Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and numerous Trump administration appointees hold financial investments in AI companies and data center developers.
Proponents of the ban argue that public lands should be protected from private commercial development and utilized to benefit the public.

source_summaries.title: I Photographed Her Parents as They Were Sentenced for Her Twin’s Death. Years Later, I Photographed Her Life.
bullets: In 2017, parents Travis and Sarah Mitchell relied on faith healing instead of medical care for their premature twins, leading to one infant's death and a prison sentence for the parents.
The surviving twin, Evelyn, was placed in the permanent care of another couple within the Followers of Christ sect, who eventually left the church.
A photojournalist who covered the original sentencing years later documented Evelyn's life, highlighting changes in Oregon law that have reduced child deaths related to faith healing.

source_summaries.title: Justices to consider disputes over transgender servicemembers, E. Jean Carroll’s jury award, and acting U.S. attorneys at next private conference
bullets: The Supreme Court will consider whether to review a lower court ruling that blocks the Trump administration from expelling transgender servicemembers from the military.

The justices will evaluate petitions related to Donald Trump's challenge of an $83.3 million jury award in the E. Jean Carroll defamation lawsuit, including claims of presidential immunity and federal substitution.
The court will decide whether to review the legality of the Trump administration's appointments of acting U.S. attorneys in Nevada and New York under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act.

source_summaries.title: Key takeaways from Monday’s order list
bullets: The Supreme Court is considering whether to review laws in Texas and Louisiana that require posting the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms.
On Monday, the court denied review in multiple cases, including challenges involving diversity requirements and Maryland's gun restrictions.
The justices invited the solicitor general to present the government's views on three lawsuits filed against the Taliban by terrorism victims.

source_summaries.title: Did Democrats blow it in Florida?
bullets: Democrats came close to winning statewide races in Florida during a massive national blue wave, sparking debates over whether they squandered a golden opportunity.
Despite a decade of losses and underinvestment in Florida, the state's congressional districts and overall ballot margins swung significantly to the left.
Questions remain over whether Florida is still too tough a political target for Democrats or if increased spending could have secured a victory.

source_summaries.title: Join us live tonight
bullets: Robert Reich is hosting a live watchalong event for the film The Work in Progress.
The film explores the transformative power of listening in a divided America.
The live event features introductions, commentary, and a Q and A session with the filmmakers and producers.

source_summaries.title: How Does Congress Stop the War
bullets: Representative Jason Crow discusses congressional oversight and the potential for the new Congress to investigate Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Crow asserts that Congress can end the ongoing war in Iran by cutting off military funding rather than continuing an endless cycle of conflict.
Recent tracking highlights potential conflicts of interest, including task force appointments holding stock in relevant pharmaceutical companies and expected presidential pardons.

source_summaries.title: Now We Act: With Senator Sheldon Whitehouse on Dark Money and a Brighter Future
bullets: Timothy Snyder hosted an unscripted conversation with Senator Sheldon Whitehouse regarding international and domestic dark money.
Senator Whitehouse has spent years working on the issue of dark money and potential transformative legislation.
The discussion highlighted how resolving the dark money problem could significantly improve the American future.

source_summaries.title: Why Sec. of Defense Pete Hegseth is the Perfect Authoritarian Tool
bullets: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is characterized as an instrument for transforming the U.S. military into an authoritarian institution.
Analyses and impeachment resolutions have cited Hegseth's far-right ideologies, misogyny, and disregard for facts as detrimental to the armed forces.
The administration's broader strategy is argued to involve converting a multiracial democracy into an autocratic ethnostate.

source_summaries.title: TAI #229: Fable 5.2 and the Case for a 2027 AI Takeoff
bullets: Leading AI researchers and industry forecasts are increasingly pointing toward a potential AI takeoff by 2027.
New model releases like Claude Fable 5.2 and Google's Gemini 4 Carbon demonstrate significant performance gains in coding and complex tasks.
Internal studies indicate that AI is now accelerating the pace of its own development through recursive self-improvement within labs like Anthropic.

source_summaries.title: A Golden State of Housing Shortages
bullets: California faces severe housing shortages and high home prices driven by restrictive zoning and environmental regulations.
The California Environmental Quality Act allows project opponents to endlessly delay construction by challenging paperwork adequacy in court.
The proposed Centennial housing project on Tejon Ranch has faced over two decades of delays and regulatory hurdles since filing initial planning documents in 2002.

source_summaries.title: Now We Act: With Rep. Sarah McBride on Care and Freedom
bullets: Timothy Snyder hosted a live, unscripted conversation with Representative Sarah McBride focusing on care and freedom.
The discussion centered on how Democrats can achieve significant political transformation on the scale of FDR or LBJ.
Snyder and McBride explored the connection between caregiving, government transformation, and achieving greater dignity and freedom.

source_summaries.title: Prof Robert Pape subscriptions for you to give away
bullets: Prof Robert Pape is offering paying subscribers five free one-month gift subscriptions to share with family and friends.
The promotional gift subscriptions have a stated value of $75.

source_summaries.source: John Ellis from Political News Items
source_summaries.title: Follow The Money.
bullets: Pollsters misjudged the mid-term elections by relying on likely-voter models that underestimated high turnout among Democrats, young voters, and nonwhite voters.
The 2026 mid-terms cannot be solely explained by turnout, as evidenced by a massive 19.5 million vote swing toward Democrats compared to 2022.
Democrats are projected to win the national House popular vote by at least 13 points, marking their best midterm margin since 1974.

source_summaries.source: Prof Robert Pape from Escalation Trap
source_summaries.title: How the Iran War Comes to American Soil — The Threat Everyone Missed
bullets: US intelligence indicates Iran is planning attacks against Trump officials in Washington, prompting increased security measures.
Six weeks prior to the report, Iran attempted an action on the soil of America's closest ally that was addressed by the Pentagon and local leadership.
The article argues that overlooked Iranian tactics could bring the ongoing conflict directly to American soil.

source_summaries.title: Tell us how to make YLE better!
bullets: Your Local Epidemiologist has opened its 2026 end-of-year reader survey to collect feedback from the community.
The survey takes less than 10 minutes and aims to help shape the newsletter's topics and formats for 2027.
Readers are asked to share their preferences, concerns about health topics, and suggestions for what the publication should change or cover more.

source_summaries.title: How Trump lost the young dudes
bullets: Young men swung dramatically from supporting Donald Trump in 2024 to voting for Democratic candidates by a wide margin in the recent midterm election.
Donald Trump's previous connection to young men through podcasts, sports culture, and a belligerent brand of masculinity proved to be a minority appeal rather than lasting loyalty.
Trump's political strategy of addressing young men's grievances ultimately failed to overcome his record of failure in office.

source_summaries.title: What Price Fame?
bullets: Fame without achievement cheapens true excellence and diminishes the value of actual accomplishment.
Tennis star Mirra Andreeva won the WTA Finals by defeating Elena Svitolina in straight sets.
Willem Dafoe delivers a career-best performance in the film Late Fame, directed by Kent Jones.

source_summaries.title: ICE may have cost Republicans more votes than inflation did in 2026
bullets: Interviews with 20,000 voters analyzed by G. Elliott Morris indicate that ICE may have cost Republicans more votes than inflation did in the 2026 midterms.
Data shows that Donald Trump's net approval rating declined significantly prior to the U.S. war against Iran, contradicting claims that the war caused a sudden structural shift in public opinion.
Public polling and survey data demonstrate that Trump's popularity fell at a steady rate both before and after the conflict began.

source_summaries.title: The Buck Stops Nowhere
bullets: President Trump refused to accept responsibility for a historic ground stop that stranded millions of travelers, blaming past administrations and congressional Democrats instead.

The article argues that Trump and his administration bear responsibility due to actions including pausing FAA funding, firing hundreds of FAA employees, and failing to fully spend previously allocated upgrade funds.
A government watchdog report had previously warned that the Trump administration's approach to replacing legacy FAA systems could cause major disruptions.
